claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed, multi-fidelity machine-learning framework can accurately predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
A small, targeted set of high-fidelity atomistic and continuum simulations is sufficient to train the proposed framework.
The surrogate will use microstructural imaging and simulation descriptors together with targeted high-fidelity simulation outputs.
The customized loss function will penalize errors in fracture toughness, elastic-property, and yield-property predictions.
Microstructural descriptors can capture the alloy’s hierarchical heterogeneity and multilevel chemical fluctuations.
These descriptors mediate a predictive link between local structural complexity and macroscopic mechanical responses.
Embedding conservation laws, aggregation behavior, and multiscale descriptors in the model bridges atomistic heterogeneity and continuum mechanical behavior.
The proposed physics-informed framework reduces reliance on computationally expensive full-scale simulations.
The framework will accurately resolve fracture-toughness behavior.
The framework will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
The framework will decrease prediction errors by approximately 15–20% compared with full high-fidelity simulations.
Physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and optimization methods have previously been used to design and screen high-entropy alloys.
Large numbers of CALPHAD calculations can make computational efficiency important for rapid alloy screening.
Complex microstructural evolution can make mechanical behavior difficult to predict and interpret.
The model will become unreliable when microstructural fluctuations or damage evolution lie outside the training distribution or are omitted from its descriptors and constraints.
The quantitative accuracy and efficiency gains depend on the quality and coverage of the descriptors and high-fidelity training data.
Ambient to moderately elevated temperatures and relevant strain rates represent realistic tensile and fracture conditions for this alloy.
